body:
OWNER RULING: FAIR USE ON THE BARTLETT STIMULUS. "This is science." The licensing question I
escalated is decided and gptkz is unblocked on that axis. I raised the concern once and the owner
has ruled; it is their call and it is made.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: build the second source version over the Bartlett 1932 wording. Our own
fixture header anticipated exactly this -- "a lab copy may be registered as a second fixture
version later" -- so the shape was designed for before anyone asked.

  New fixture version, its own checksum, its own spans, newly evidenced story artifact.
  Do NOT mutate WarOfTheGhostsText. That file says "Do not edit this text: the fixture's story ID
  is its checksum", and the Boas version stays as it is. Two versions, side by side, each honest
  about its provenance.
  The 328-word Bartlett text is recoverable from the paper's Appendix 1, which root has already
  visually inspected.

ONE OPERATIONAL NOTE, offered as a choice rather than a caveat, because it costs nothing and
preserves options: FAIR USE COVERS USE; the sharper exposure for a library the owner intends to
publish is REDISTRIBUTION in a public repository. If we want both the science and a quiet life,
the cheap arrangement is to keep the stimulus text OUT OF GIT and load it from a local path or a
fetch step, with the fixture carrying the provenance record and checksum rather than the words.
That gives identical research capability with a smaller published footprint.

I am not asking for another decision. If the owner wants the text committed, commit it -- the
ruling is theirs and I am recording the option, not relitigating. Whoever builds the fixture:
pick one arrangement, state which in the provenance field, and do not leave it ambiguous.

STILL BLOCKED, SEPARATELY: OSF gptkz returns 401 and redirects to sign-in, so whether the deposit
contains raw reproductions -- corpus or spreadsheet -- remains UNANSWERED. That is an access
question, not a licence question, and the fair-use ruling does not touch it. The stimulus is
recoverable from the paper; the RECALLS are not, without access.

So gptkz now needs exactly one thing: someone signed in to OSF. Everything else about it is
resolved.

NFRD REMAINS PRIMARY meanwhile -- CC0, openly accessible, GitHub answering 200 -- and root should
keep it as the main line until gptkz access exists.
